front: What are the two fixed points of the Celsius scale?
back: Ice point 0 °C (pure melting ice) and steam point 100 °C (steam at standard pressure).
A measurable property that changes with temperature (e.g. length of a liquid column, resistance, emf).

front: What makes a liquid-in-glass thermometer sensitive?
back: A large bulb and a narrow bore.

front: Why does a clinical thermometer have a constriction?
back: It stops the liquid falling back, so the maximum reading stays.
Very wide range, quick response, small; but it needs a voltmeter.

front: Mercury or alcohol for very cold places?
back: Alcohol: it freezes at about −115 °C; mercury freezes at −39 °C.
